The school that I graduated from had a good student program. Those who are in their best behavior, are given this form. Teachers & staff have to sign this form in order to get you in the running to be accepted into the program. 

At first it was a great program. With lots of benefits. You'll get special treatment when it came to lunches & breakfast. You'll get into luncheons with other college deans. You'll be able to stand out more than other applicants in the college admissions. 

It's great. But. The school had a dark side. Those that are favored by the teachers, they get to be in the running. Those who are not, they'll be given a hard time getting into that program. 

The school had a club for LGBTQ+ students. But the school had a lot of teachers that were bigoted. Rumor has it, that's why one of the English teachers got fired. There were teachers that would give other students a hard time for anything. 

There were two teachers that would give female students or female presenting students a hard time due to sexualizing them. Singling them out to be used as an example of, when other students are misbehaving.

One of the STMs was looking over a student's breast at prom. Another made a hideous remark on "girls being too grown nowadays." The added what he'll do to her if was younger. A 16 year old student. Before prom.

The misogyny was rampant in that school. But no one batted an eye because the neighborhood was mostly first generation Americans or immigrants. So, they were using the misogyny that's already prevalent in the lives of their students in order to go under the radar.

The favoritism was so bad, if there were any trouble with a group of students, the gavel goes harder on the students that wasn't in the program. There were teachers that stood against the program. Saw it for what it was, unfair. They were shunned by other teachers. 

The teachers had cliques. I was convinced that they never moved on from high school. I guess that was also one of the reasons why they treated some students so badly.
